title: Defect-cavity narrowband filter with relaxed bounds and unfrozen interfaces
scientific_hypothesis: A 29-layer Ta2O5/SiO2 stack with a central defect cavity, when initialized at quarter-wave optical thicknesses near 1550 nm and optimized with relaxed thickness bounds [30, 450] nm on cavity-adjacent layers, will produce a resonant transmission peak at 1550 nm with mean transmittance above 0.90 while maintaining mean transmittance below 0.10 in the 1400-1500 nm and 1600-1700 nm stopbands.
design_principle: Recalled from thin-film optics practice: a defect layer (optical thickness deviating from quarter-wave) embedded in a periodic Bragg mirror creates a localized state within the photonic bandgap, allowing narrowband transmission. The mirror pairs on either side provide high reflectance outside the resonance. Quarter-wave initialization places the design near a known resonant basin, and gradient optimization refines thicknesses to balance passband transmission against stopband rejection.
proposed_topology: 29 explicit layers: Ta2O5/SiO2/Ta2O5/SiO2/Ta2O5/SiO2/Ta2O5/SiO2/Ta2O5/SiO2/Ta2O5/SiO2/Ta2O5/SiO2/Ta2O5/SiO2/Ta2O5/SiO2/Ta2O5/SiO2/Ta2O5/SiO2/Ta2O5/SiO2/Ta2O5/SiO2/Ta2O5/SiO2/Ta2O5, with layer 15 (Ta2O5) serving as the central defect cavity, incident medium air, substrate fused silica.
design_variables: individual layer thicknesses for all 29 layers
thickness bounds relaxed to [30, 450] nm for layers 13-17
layers 11-13 and 17-19 unfrozen to allow cavity-mirror interface adjustment
soft_objectives: maximize mean transmittance in 1545-1555 nm passband
minimize mean transmittance in 1400-1500 nm stopband
minimize mean transmittance in 1600-1700 nm stopband
manufacturing_considerations: total layer count fixed at 29 (under 30-layer limit)
thickness bounds [30, 450] nm chosen to remain within typical deposition control ranges
alternating high/low index materials simplify process monitoring
theory_basis: Recalled: defect-cavity filters produce narrow transmission peaks within a DBR stopband
Recalled: quarter-wave optical thickness initialization (λ/4n) places designs near resonant solutions
Recalled: Ta2O5 has higher refractive index than SiO2 in the near-infrared, enabling high-contrast Bragg mirrors
Recalled: gradient-based thickness optimization can refine initial quarter-wave designs to improve spectral performance
Recalled: relaxing bounds on cavity-adjacent layers allows the optimizer to adjust the effective cavity length and mirror coupling
expected_advantages: Narrow passband centered at 1550 nm suitable for coherent LiDAR
Strong stopband rejection reduces solar background interference
29 layers provides sufficient mirror pairs for high out-of-band suppression while staying under the 30-layer manufacturing constraint
Quarter-wave seeding reduces optimization iterations needed to reach a resonant solution
known_risks: Uncertain: exact n/k values for Ta2O5 at 1550 nm - would need to verify against material_catalog registry data
Uncertain: whether 29 layers provides enough stopband rejection for the 1400-1500 nm and 1600-1700 nm bands - may need more pairs if rejection is insufficient
Uncertain: stress accumulation in 29-layer Ta2O5/SiO2 stacks - would need process data to confirm manufacturability
Uncertain: bandwidth of the resonant peak - quarter-wave defect may produce narrower passband than desired for LiDAR tolerance

execution_request_english: Design a 29-layer planar dielectric filter for 1550 nm LiDAR receiver. Incident medium: air. Substrate: fused silica. Materials: Ta2O5 (Gao) (high index) and SiO2 (Lemarchand) (low index), alternating sequence starting with Ta2O5 (Gao) at the air side. Layer sequence: Ta2O5 (Gao)/SiO2 (Lemarchand)/Ta2O5 (Gao)/SiO2 (Lemarchand)/Ta2O5 (Gao)/SiO2 (Lemarchand)/Ta2O5 (Gao)/SiO2 (Lemarchand)/Ta2O5 (Gao)/SiO2 (Lemarchand)/Ta2O5 (Gao)/SiO2 (Lemarchand)/Ta2O5 (Gao)/SiO2 (Lemarchand)/Ta2O5 (Gao)/SiO2 (Lemarchand)/Ta2O5 (Gao)/SiO2 (Lemarchand)/Ta2O5 (Gao)/SiO2 (Lemarchand)/Ta2O5 (Gao)/SiO2 (Lemarchand)/Ta2O5 (Gao)/SiO2 (Lemarchand)/Ta2O5 (Gao)/SiO2 (Lemarchand)/Ta2O5 (Gao)/SiO2 (Lemarchand)/Ta2O5 (Gao) (29 layers total, layer 15 is the central defect). Initialize all layer thicknesses at quarter-wave optical thickness at 1550 nm (Ta2O5 (Gao): approximately 1550/(4*n_Ta2O5 (Gao)), SiO2 (Lemarchand): approximately 1550/(4*n_SiO2 (Lemarchand))). Set thickness bounds to [30, 450] nm for layers 13-17 (cavity region), and [50, 400] nm for all other layers. Allow all 29 layer thicknesses to be optimized via gradient-based methods. Optimization objectives: maximize mean transmittance over 1545-1555 nm wavelength band, minimize mean transmittance over 1400-1500 nm band, minimize mean transmittance over 1600-1700 nm band. Use coherent transfer-matrix method at normal incidence. Simulation wavelength grid must span 1400-1700 nm with sufficient resolution to resolve the narrow passband.
revision_reason: Repair compilation failure from iteration 23 (target band does not overlap simulation grid). Applied pre-declared repair: relaxed layers 13-17 bounds from [50, 400] nm to [30, 450] nm, unfrozen layers 11-13 and 17-19 to restore cavity-mirror interface compliance, re-seeded cavity optical thicknesses at quarter-wave approximation centered at 1550 nm to place initial population inside resonant basin.
